reviews.title: Overall a great upgrade to freshen up your old desktop.
reviews.comment: I purchased this ram to upgrade my old dell computer. The RAM works great and this kit maxed the computer out on RAM. I tried to use two of my old ram sticks to go over 64GB but the bios would not allow the OS to use the memory above 64GB. This is a bios issue not a problem with the memory. The specs for my processor say that it is capable of 128GB of memory, but Dell never provided the BIOS for this upgrade. So check with the BIOS vendor to make sure it will work if you're not sure. Anyway, overall its a great upgrade to freshen up your old desktop.
reviews.author: CBW

reviews.title: DOA — None of the 4 sticks would POST
reviews.comment: Purchased the 128GB kit (4x32GB) for an ASUS ROG STRIX B550-F Gaming WiFi II with a Ryzen 9 5950X. None of the four sticks would boot the system. Tested each stick individually in the primary DIMM slot after a full CMOS clear. Solid yellow DRAM LED every time, no POST. Put my old G.Skill Ripjaws V back in the same slot and the system booted immediately. The kit also arrived as two separate 64GB (2x32GB) clamshells rather than a matched quad kit, despite the listing advertising a 128GB 4x32GB kit. Worse, the failed boot attempts corrupted my motherboard's memory training data, which temporarily prevented even my known-good RAM from working until I shorted the CLRTC pins to force a full BIOS reset. So this product didn't just not work — it actively created additional problems I had to spend hours fixing. The package included a card urging buyers to contact the seller directly before leaving negative feedback. I'd recommend ignoring that and going straight through Amazon's return process.
reviews.author: Noah Dawson
